# UICC, USIM and the card interface: compliance register

What this is: the requirements of this area that are built and verified against running code, the typed rows recorded while building them, and coverage counts derived from the specs (verification.md §5). Requirements are in [`requirements.md`](../../requirements.md); deviations in [`deviations.md`](../deviations.md).

Specs read: TS 102.221 18.04.00, TS 31.101 j00, TS 31.102 j60.

Row suffixes (requirements.md): -D defect in the sim, -B a choice the spec leaves open, -G declared gap, -V deviation from a "shall", -S spec contradiction and the reading chosen, -M mutant, -T T0 reading or measurement, -F a kaluza-core defect the sim found, -X retired. Verification: U unit, KAT or oracle test; F fuzz or property test; I interop; L lab; G gate row; A real-device comparison.

## Typed rows

| Row | Date | What | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| KS-UICC-T1 | 2026-10-14 | M12 check of every v1 APDU type (16 commands) and FCP templates (MF, ADF, DF, transparent, linear fixed, cyclic and BER-TLV EFs): 25 command/response pairs and 7 templates written from ETSI TS 102 221 clauses 10 and 11 and TS 31.102 clause 7 (PINs, keys and the SUCI of a test-range IMSI are synthetic). Ours decodes and re-encodes byte for byte; pySim (run out of process in its own venv, a GPL program used like tshark, nothing of it copied) reads the same command, parameters, P3, response and status word, and the same FCP data objects in the same order; tshark's gsm_sim, from a GSMTAP SIM frame, finds nothing wrong and shows our INS, parameters, record, offset, Lc/Le, AUTHENTICATE context and values, and status word. 32 checks, all PASS | build/oracle/m12roundtrip.tsv, tests/oracles/ksimoracle/m12rt.py, tests/oracles/pysim_helper.py, M12 |
| KS-UICC-T2 | 2026-10-14 | Oracle defects seen in M12. pySim computes a READ/UPDATE BINARY offset as ((P1 & 0x7F) << 8) & P2 where TS 102 221 11.1.3.2 means P1's low bits and P2 together (an OR): its reading is checked against its own formula and tshark's bin_offset against ours (they agree). tshark 4.6.4 reads a P3 of '00' (Le 256) and the next octet as a two-octet extended Le, so Le 256 is not compared with it. Both worth reporting upstream; neither changes our reading | tests/oracles/ksimoracle/m12rt.py, M12 |
| KS-UICC-B1 | 2026-10-14 | APDUs are short form only (TS 102 221 has no extended lengths: an Lc of '00' followed by more octets is unsupported). The class byte follows tables 10.3 and 10.4a (channels 0-19, chaining refused) and the command name table 10.5 with the class coding it allows. Key material stays out of the codec layer, which must stay pure (R3): AUTHENTICATE's reader returns where CK, IK and Kc sit in the response for the caller to copy into SecretBytes, and its writers take them as views the caller exposes; to_json shows keys and PIN, PUK and ADM values by length only, and also a GET RESPONSE that returns an AUTHENTICATE result. The PIN status template 'C6' is read as a template though its tag's constructed bit is clear (11.1.1.4.10) | src/codec/uicc/apdu.hpp, src/codec/uicc/fcp.hpp, tests/unit/uicc/uicc_test.cpp, M12 |
| KS-UICC-G1 | 2026-10-14 | No independent-producer APDU or FCP vectors in P0: the values are generated from the specs and checked by pySim and tshark. Real card exchanges come with the card bridge in P1 (same decision as KS-PLAT-G2). Not read below the parameter level in P0: AUTHENTICATE with the odd INS ('89', BER-TLV chained), the GBA, MBMS and VGCS contexts, and the commands outside v1 (table 10.5 names them) | build/oracle/m12roundtrip.tsv, M12 |
| KS-UICC-T3 | 2026-10-15 | TS 31.102 j60 re-check of the card files of sim-uicc.md section 3 (owed since the design, done in P1 N0). Every ADF.USIM file id matches its clause 4.2.x (6F07 IMSI, 6FAD AD, 6F38 UST, 6F56 EST, 6F08 Keys, 6F09 KeysPS, 6F7E LOCI, 6F73 PSLOCI, 6F7B FPLMN, 6F31 HPPLMN, 6F60 PLMNwAcT, 6F61 OPLMNwACT, 6F62 HPLMNwAcT, 6FD9 EHPLMN, 6F78 ACC, 6F46 SPN, 6F40 MSISDN, 6F3C SMS, 6F42 SMSP, 6F43 SMSS, 6F06 ARR, 6F5B START-HFN, 6F5C THRESHOLD); DF5GS is '5FC0' and its files match 4.4.11.x (4F01 and 4F03 service 122, 4F05 123, 4F06 126, 4F07 124, 4F08 129, 4F09 130, 4F0A 124). The MF files match ETSI TS 102 221 V18.4.0 13.1-13.4 (2F00 DIR, 2FE2 ICCID, 2F05 PL, 2F06 ARR). Two additions the design table missed: 4.2.8 requires service 133 (5G Security Parameters extended) to be available whenever 123 is, so a card template with 4F05 sets both; 4F03 also names service 136 (several NAS security context records for multiple registration) and 4F09 service 146 (NID), both optional and left unset in P1 | spec/3gpp/31/31102-j60 (4.2, 4.2.8, 4.4.11), spec/etsi/ts_102221v180400p.pdf 13; docs/sim-uicc.md 3; P1 N0 |
